question.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+xy)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+xy)\,j \\  & =(2x+y)\,i+x\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t+1$ and $y=-{t}^{2}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(2t+2-{t}^{2})\,i+(t+1)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2})\,j \\  & =\,i-2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((2t+2-{t}^{2})\,i+(t+1)\,j)\cdot (\,i-2t\,j) \\  & =2t+2-{t}^{2}-2t(t+1) \\  & =2t+2-{t}^{2}-2{t}^{2}-2t \\  & =2-3{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
